$comment: Declares what the renderer emits and under what conditions. Inclusion is decided HERE rather than inside templates, so a template file stays valid HCL/YAML/Markdown on its own and factory CI can run `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` against the raw corpus. Conditions use the same tiny expression grammar as the #{{IF}} directives: path, !path, defined path, path == 'v', path != 'v', path contains 'v', joined by && and ||.
$statusComment: Stage 6 promoted the real Terraform corpus. Five live layers are emitted from templates (global, platform-connectivity, platform-management, workloads-prod, sandbox) and the module corpus is copied verbatim. Two layers Get-LzActiveLayers can select — platform-identity and workloads-nonprod — have no source under terraform/live and are therefore not emitted; guard G21 refuses a render that would select one, rather than shipping a layer directory containing only a backend. Stage 7 workflow corpus is registered here.

Hub identifiers. This is the contract the workload layers read through remote state.
Connectivity layer variables. Omitted entirely when no platform networking is deployed.

Backup baseline and sandbox-cleanup automation. Both sections are conditional.
Vault and automation identifiers, matching whichever sections main.tf emitted.
Management layer variables.

Production workload layer variables.

A single time-boxed resource group. Nothing in it varies with configuration.

perLayerFiles.description: Backend configuration, rendered once per active layer. Each layer keeps an isolated state file — layers are never merged (control AR3).

$directoriesComment: Whole-tree copies. The module corpus is dozens of static files with no per-configuration variation; listing each one here would add no decision while creating a trap where a newly added .tf is silently not shipped. Anything that DOES vary belongs in `files`, where its condition is visible. `exclude` patterns are matched against the path relative to `source`, with forward slashes.

directories.description: The reusable module corpus, copied verbatim. Lock files are excluded because a dependency lock is only meaningful at the root module; the ones under modules/ are leftovers from running terraform inside a module directory and would mislead anyone who trusted them. The two scaffold modules are excluded here and re-added below only when the feature that needs them is enabled.
Scaffold module. Guard G02 refuses to render at all when Sentinel is enabled and this module is still scaffold-only, so reaching this entry means it has been implemented.
Scaffold module. Guard G03 covers it the way G02 covers sentinel-siem.
Runbook content the platform-management layer loads with file(). Emitted only alongside the automation that reads it — file() resolves at plan time, so a missing script fails the plan, not the apply.
